nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant has aborted, then the coordinator has not decided commit.
nodes.title: An aborted participant rules out a coordinator commit

nodes.summary: The actions of the two-phase commit protocol over a set $P$ of participants are: a participant $p \in P$ votes yes; a participant $p$ votes no; the coordinator decides commit; the coordinator decides abort; a participant $p$ learns the commit decision; and a participant $p$ learns the abort decision.
nodes.title: Two-phase commit actions

nodes.summary: For every set $P$ of participants, in every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant $p$ has committed, then no participant $q$ has aborted.
nodes.title: Atomicity between participants

nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant has committed, then every participant voted yes, that is, every participant is prepared or committed.
nodes.title: Validity for participants

nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if the coordinator has decided abort, then no participant has committed.
nodes.title: An aborted coordinator has no committed participant

nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if the coordinator has decided commit, then every participant voted yes, that is, every participant is prepared or committed.
nodes.title: Validity for the coordinator

nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if the coordinator has decided commit, then no participant has aborted.
nodes.title: A committed coordinator has no aborted participant

nodes.summary: In two-phase commit the coordinator is in one of three states: waiting (collecting votes), committed (it has decided commit) or aborted (it has decided abort).
nodes.title: Coordinator states

nodes.summary: The initial state of the two-phase commit protocol: the coordinator is waiting and every participant is working.
nodes.title: Initial state of two-phase commit

nodes.summary: If a state $s$ of the two-phase commit protocol satisfies the inductive invariant and a state $t$ is reached from $s$ by a finite sequence of transitions, then $t$ satisfies the invariant.
nodes.title: Multistep transitions preserve the two-phase commit invariant

nodes.summary: For every set $P$ of participants, every global state of the two-phase commit protocol that is reachable from the initial state satisfies the inductive invariant, that is, both of the following hold: if the coordinator has committed, then every participant is prepared or committed; and every committed participant has a committed coordinator.
nodes.title: The two-phase commit invariant holds in reachable states

nodes.summary: A global state $s$ of the two-phase commit protocol satisfies the invariant when two conditions hold: if the coordinator has committed, then every participant is prepared or committed; and every committed participant has a committed coordinator.
nodes.title: Two-phase commit invariant

nodes.summary: For a set $P$ of participants, the labelled transition system whose states are the global states of the protocol, whose labels are the protocol actions, and whose transitions are the protocol steps.
nodes.title: Two-phase commit as a transition system

nodes.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant has committed, then the coordinator has committed.
nodes.title: A committed participant has a committed coordinator

nodes.summary: A participant is in one of four states: working (it has not voted), prepared (it voted yes and waits for the decision), committed, or aborted (it voted no, or learned of an abort).
nodes.title: Participant states in two-phase commit

nodes.summary: A global state $s$ is reachable when some finite sequence of protocol actions leads by protocol steps from the initial state, in which the coordinator is waiting and every participant is working, to $s$.
nodes.title: Reachable states of two-phase commit

nodes.summary: For a global state $s$, a participant $p$ and a participant state $x$, the updated state has the same coordinator state as $s$, gives participant $p$ the state $x$, and leaves the state of every other participant unchanged.
nodes.title: Updating one participant's state

nodes.summary: For a set $P$ of participants, a global state consists of a coordinator state together with a participant state for each participant $p \in P$.
nodes.title: Global states of two-phase commit

nodes.summary: If a global state $s$ of the two-phase commit protocol is reachable and some action takes $s$ to $t$ in one protocol step, then $t$ is reachable.
nodes.title: Reachable states are closed under steps

nodes.summary: The protocol steps from a global state $s$ to a global state $t$ by an action exactly in the following cases. A working participant $p$ may vote yes, after which $p$ is prepared, or vote no, after which $p$ is aborted. nodes.title: Transitions of two-phase commit

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
